newsitem.title: INDIA: RESEARCH ALERT-Kotak downgrades India ACC.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Kotak downgrades India ACC.

text.p: Kotak Securities said on Tuesday it was downgrading its rating on shares of India's largest cement maker Associate Cement Companies (ACC) to market performer from market outperformer.
"We have modified our forecasts based on newly-released balance sheet data and recent meetings with management," Kotak, the Indian associate of Goldman Sachs, said in a report.
The share fell by over 6.0 percent this week on the National Stock Exchange. On Tuesday, ACC shares closed at 1,850 rupees, down 47 rupees from the previous close.
It said it revised its earnings per share estimate on fully diluted equity for 1996/97 (April-March) to 170 rupees from 187 and for 1997/98 to 198 rupees from 225.
"Our lower estimates reflect several, largely unrelated issues," Kotak analyst Sanjeev Joshi said.

"Significantly, and this is a source of some longer term comfort, some of the macro issues that have recently haunted the Indian cement industry -- overcapacity, input cost increases putting pressure on margings -- are not the main cause of our revisions," it said.

"A slightly swifter capital spending programme, a slightly higher working capital requirement and some non-payment of the final tranche of a rights issue conspired to reduce the free cash flow," the Kotak report said.
This increases ACC's net debt entering fiscal 1997 and, hence, will increase interest expense for the full year, it said. It said the free cash flow was less than what it had expected earlier.
